title: Plot-level initial biomass, composition, and fitted field-retention parameters for fresh roadside cuttings
license: Not stated in accessible article metadata; page marks article Free Access. Dataset is a limited factual transcription of published numeric results; redistribution rights should not be inferred.
geography: Roadside locations in the middle and eastern Netherlands
source_location: Tables 1 and 3; Journal of Applied Ecology 35(3), pp. 349–364

units_and_basis.biomass_t_dm_per_ha: t dry matter per hectare at cutting
units_and_basis.n_mg_per_g_dm: mg N per g dry matter (numerically equal to g/kg DM)
units_and_basis.p_mg_per_g_dm: mg P per g dry matter
units_and_basis.k_mg_per_g_dm: mg K per g dry matter
units_and_basis.c_mg_per_g_dm: mg C per g dry matter
units_and_basis.*_asymptotic_fraction: dimensionless fitted asymptotic remaining fraction a
units_and_basis.*_k_per_week: fitted rate parameter k in week^-1, for Y(t)=a+(1-a)exp(-kt), t in weeks
units_and_basis.*_fit_r2: coefficient of determination of source-reported fit

study_conditions.field_period: 24 May to 6 July 1993; cutting dates varied by site between 24 May and 8 June
study_conditions.cuttings: Fresh material cut at 1 cm, chopped to <=10 cm, mixed, and placed in 1 mm mesh litterbags in the field
study_conditions.sampling: Five litterbags per plot per sampling set; sampled at 1–2 week intervals over 4–6 weeks
study_conditions.weather_context: Mean air temperature approximately 16 °C; 75 mm rainfall over 43 days at the nearby weather station
study_conditions.model: Source fit: Y(t)=a+(1-a)exp(-kt), where Y is remaining fraction and t is weeks since cutting

data_handling: Tables 1 and 3 transcribed at printed precision. Source-reported missing/failed-fit fields are blank. No interpolation, averaging, refitting, unit conversion, or model activation was performed.
limitations: This describes fresh cuttings left in field conditions before collection, not stored silage, ensiled biomass, or the GreenHub plant's storage process.
The study is one 1993 short-term field campaign and has only eight plots: seven in two grassland communities and one contrasting grass-heath plot.

Table 3 coefficients are fitted parameters, not raw time-series measurements. Fit quality varies; Rossum east N parameters are specially flagged by the source as uncertain, and several other N fits are weak.
The paper's broader regression/projection figures are not transcribed here. No harvested-versus-left-behind mass balance or collected feed quantity is inferred.
Do not apply these coefficients as GreenHub storage defaults or combine field losses with silage-storage loss estimates without a defined sequential boundary.
